frequency_question: How often do structural frictions from intermediary pushback successfully delay or cancel scheduled financial transaction fee rules within the stipulated implementation window?
membership_rule: Members are central government or central bank announcements of merchant discount rates or digital transaction fee changes that face coordinated merchant/ecosystem resistance. Excluded are voluntary guidelines or non-binding consultations.

cases.name: RBI Discussion Paper on Charges in Payment Systems pushback (2022)
Deferred implementation of credit card MDR caps in other major emerging markets (e.g., Brazil interchange caps phased rollout)
Delayed enforcement of data localization directives under similar structural pressure in India

coverage_note: 4 prominent cases named covering the relevant regulatory class in the jurisdiction.
known_gaps: Excludes minor unpublicized deferrals negotiated bilaterally behind closed doors.
skeleton: Total contested digital payment regulatory rollouts in India over the past 6 years vs. those successfully delayed or halted by structural/intermediary friction prior to the deadline.
multiplier: 1 hit out of 4 documented major contested payment fee/infrastructure implementation attempts where friction successfully altered the scheduled timeline.
validity_reason: The institutional framework governing digital payments in the jurisdiction remains stable under the current central bank and finance ministry structure through the medium term.
